mfg1-electrical-l043.title: The two exam sections and your study plan
mfg1-electrical-l043.objective: Assess theory and practical results separately, and learn Japanese alongside technical knowledge.

paragraphs.title: Manage the two times separately
paragraphs.text: The uploaded textbook describes the July 2026 format: theory has 30 true/false questions in 40 minutes; practical has 10 multiple-choice judgment and planning questions in 40 minutes. The respective passing rates are 65% and 60%, and both sections must meet their own threshold. This means at least 20 of 30 and 6 of 10 correct.

paragraphs.title: Relating the category to work
paragraphs.text: Electrical/electronic assembly study includes machining, maintenance, packaging, plastics, and circuit boards as well as wiring and circuits. Passing the exam is different from qualifications, training, and company authorization to operate a particular machine. Check the official application guidance for eligibility and what to bring.

paragraphs.title: Understand the original Japanese before practicing
paragraphs.text: Read terms, units, and negative wording through to the end. Do not record, remove, or share exam-site questions or answers; this app uses newly written practice questions. Record why you struggle and move to timed practice after you can explain the material.

terms.meaning: A method that judges whether a statement is true or false.
A format in which an answer is selected from several choices.
The performance requirements that each section must meet.
Wording such as “do not” or “is not” that negates meaning.

mfg1-electrical-l043.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Judge theory 19/30 and practical 8/10 separately against their thresholds. Explain your process for learning technical terms and where to verify exam information.
safety: Do not treat study or passing an exam as authorization to operate real equipment.
mfg1-electrical-l043.summary: Assess theory and practical results separately, and learn Japanese alongside technical knowledge.

mfg1-electrical-l044.title: Safety and health responsibilities and responses to abnormalities
mfg1-electrical-l044.objective: Know roles and procedures, and report abnormalities specifically.

paragraphs.title: A system that protects people and health
paragraphs.text: Heat, heavy objects, machines, and chemicals present different hazards. Occupational safety and health covers disease prevention as well as injuries. Combine the company’s management responsibilities with workers’ compliance to reduce danger to everyone nearby.

paragraphs.title: Know workplace roles
paragraphs.text: The safety and health committee discusses issues; safety managers and occupational physicians have their own specialist roles. Requirements are not identical at every workplace. Confirm whom to consult, emergency contacts, and the chain of command in your own workplace.

paragraphs.title: Do not hide abnormalities
paragraphs.text: If sound, smell, or vibration differs from normal, follow your assigned procedure for stopping, evacuation, and reporting. Do not touch unfamiliar machines without authorization or throw tools to others; return them to their designated place. Do not skip procedures simply because danger is not visible.

terms.meaning: Activities protecting workers’ safety and health.
A physician who supports health management at work.
The links between roles that give instructions and receive reports.
A condition differing from the specified or usual state.

mfg1-electrical-l044.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Describe discovery, making the situation safe, reporting, and authorization after finding an unusual noise. Make a table of the people whose responsibilities you need to confirm.
safety: Do not enter a hazardous area without authorization to investigate or rescue someone.
mfg1-electrical-l044.summary: Know roles and procedures, and report abnormalities specifically.

mfg1-electrical-l045.title: Use 5S and the three fixed conditions to detect shortages and mixing
mfg1-electrical-l045.objective: Maintain 5S and make item and quantity deviations visible with the three fixed conditions.

paragraphs.title: Distinguish five actions
paragraphs.text: Sorting separates needed from unneeded things and removes the latter. Setting in order places needed items for convenient use; cleaning removes dirt. Standardized cleanliness maintains sorting, order, and cleaning, while discipline makes agreed behavior habitual.

paragraphs.title: Specify location, item, and quantity
paragraphs.text: The three fixed conditions specify location, item, and quantity. Mark not just the shelf position but also the part number and permitted quantity there. Upper and lower limits help reveal shortages, excess stock, and mixed items.

paragraphs.title: Tidying is not authorization to discard
paragraphs.text: Do not discard unidentified or held items yourself; identify them and ask the responsible person. If another item is in terminalB’s shelf location, merely moving it to a vacant space does not prevent recurrence. Compare labels and records and investigate why it was mixed in.

terms.meaning: Separating needed from unneeded items and removing the latter.
Maintaining the state achieved by sorting, order, and cleaning.
Management that specifies location, item, and quantity.
Setting and observing a quantity or permitted range.

mfg1-electrical-l045.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Make a terminal-shelf checklist specifying location, part number, a lower limit of 8 and upper limit of 24. Separately report a stock of 5 and the presence of a different item.
safety: Do not independently classify chemicals or held items as unnecessary and dispose of them.
mfg1-electrical-l045.summary: Maintain 5S and make item and quantity deviations visible with the three fixed conditions.

mfg1-electrical-l046.title: Confirm training and select protection for the task
mfg1-electrical-l046.objective: Check training requirements and responsibility; match protective equipment to the hazard.

paragraphs.title: Learn before a new assignment
paragraphs.text: On hiring or a change of duties, confirm hazards, equipment, protective equipment, procedures, startup checks, and emergency responses. The qualifications, skills courses, or special education needed for hazardous work depend on the actual conditions. The task name alone does not establish whether you may do it.

paragraphs.title: OJT is not leaving someone to learn alone
paragraphs.text: Check the instructor’s explanation and demonstration, practice within the approved scope, and receive feedback. Do not pretend to understand after merely watching; explain essential steps in your own words. Receiving OJT does not automatically replace statutory training or qualifications.

paragraphs.title: Select for each hazard
paragraphs.text: Safety footwear addresses hazards such as falling objects; protective glasses address flying material. Gloves can protect or create entanglement hazards, depending on the task. Keep gloved hands away from a rotating drill press, and confirm chemical-compatible protection and ventilation for chemical work. For transport, check weight, visibility, route, and specified aids, avoiding suspended loads and their surroundings. Near casting work, distinguish heat from dust and check heat-illness measures and suitable dust protection.

terms.meaning: Safety and health education required for certain hazardous work.
Training through explanation, practice, and advice during actual work.
Equipment that protects eyes from flying material and similar hazards.
Clothing or body parts being pulled into rotating machinery.

mfg1-electrical-l046.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Prepare questions about training, authorized scope, protection, inspection, and emergency contacts before taking charge of new equipment. Compare glove decisions for rotating work and chemical handling.
safety: Do not independently operate dangerous machinery merely because you have training and protective equipment.
mfg1-electrical-l046.summary: Check training requirements and responsibility; match protective equipment to the hazard.

mfg1-electrical-l047.title: Read prohibition, warning, and evacuation signs separately
mfg1-electrical-l047.objective: Read the target, area, and disaster type as well as the color and shape.

paragraphs.title: Actions that are forbidden
paragraphs.text: Red prohibition signs include no smoking, no flames, no entry, do not touch, and not for drinking. Read a general prohibition symbol with its accompanying target. Confirm what is restricted, such as people entering versus vehicles entering.

paragraphs.title: Recognize the presence of danger
paragraphs.text: Yellow warning signs include electric shock, slipping, steps, falls, and overhead obstacles. A warning rather than a prohibition does not automatically grant free entry. Check the area, work conditions, and accompanying instructions, and describe hazards specifically.

paragraphs.title: Know emergency locations
paragraphs.text: Extinguisher, AED, and evacuation signs help locate equipment and destinations. Do not treat a wide-area evacuation location, evacuation building, and tsunami refuge as identical; match the disaster type with workplace routes. When using an AED, follow its voice guidance and emergency responders’ instructions.

terms.meaning: An instruction that a specified action must not be performed.
A sign indicating the presence of a hazard.
Moving away from danger to a safe location.
A device that analyzes heart rhythm and guides an electric shock when needed.

mfg1-electrical-l047.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Match workplace electric-shock, extinguisher, and refuge signs with their meanings and checks. Describe conditions for choosing between two different evacuation destinations.
safety: Do not enter a prohibited area merely to inspect its signs.
mfg1-electrical-l047.summary: Read the target, area, and disaster type as well as the color and shape.

mfg1-electrical-l048.title: Connect SDS information and chemical labels to work
mfg1-electrical-l048.objective: Match the label with the SDS and check ventilation, protection, and emergency responses beforehand.

paragraphs.title: Pictograms are clues to hazards
paragraphs.text: Flame, corrosion, health hazard, environmental hazard, and exclamation-mark symbols indicate different hazards. One container may present several. Do not infer all concentrations, protection, or first aid from the picture alone; match the product identification on the label and SDS.

paragraphs.title: Read the necessary sections before use
paragraphs.text: An SDS includes hazards, handling and storage, exposure prevention, first aid, and spill response. Operate local exhaust or ventilation and confirm compatible protective equipment and waste-liquid containers. Follow the responsible person’s guidance for health management such as special medical examinations.

paragraphs.title: Do not guess what an unknown liquid is
paragraphs.text: Do not identify an unlabeled decanted liquid by color or smell; suspend use. Vapor can accumulate in tanks handling organic solvents, so cleaning is not a task to undertake independently. Decanting, mixing, and spill response require approved procedures.

terms.meaning: A safety data sheet describing chemical hazards and handling information.
Being subjected to harmful substances through inhalation, skin contact, or similar routes.
Equipment that extracts harmful air near its source.
The ability to damage skin, metals, or similar materials.

mfg1-electrical-l048.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
For a cleaning liquid with an unreadable label, organize five checks: product identity, SDS, ventilation, protection, and waste handling. Write a report suspending use.
safety: Do not identify chemicals by smelling or mixing them. Do not enter tanks without authorization.
mfg1-electrical-l048.summary: Match the label with the SDS and check ventilation, protection, and emergency responses beforehand.

mfg1-electrical-l049.title: Near misses and improvement through OSHMS
mfg1-electrical-l049.objective: Share warning events even without injury and continue evaluating countermeasures.

paragraphs.title: Report small warning events
paragraphs.text: Learn Heinrich’s 1:29:300 as a way of considering serious accidents, minor accidents, and near misses. It does not guarantee these counts at every site or mean that work is safe until 300 events. Record dangerous approaches or almost-falling objects even without injury.

paragraphs.title: Improve as an organization
paragraphs.text: OSHMS repeatedly plans, implements, evaluates, and improves safety and health management. Evaluate effects and remaining risks, assign responsibility and deadlines, and revise. Producing records alone does not complete the activity.

paragraphs.title: Do not claim absolute safety
paragraphs.text: Anticipate machine failure, human error, and natural disasters, and continue reducing danger as far as possible. Check that a measure has not created a new hazard. Combine actions selected in hazard prediction with changes to equipment or processes.

terms.meaning: An event that did not cause an accident but revealed danger.

terms.reading: おーえすえいちえむえす
terms.meaning: A system for continually managing safety and health.
Risk that remains after countermeasures.
Reflecting evaluated problems in subsequent actions or plans.

mfg1-electrical-l049.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Record an almost-falling part near someone’s foot as facts, despite no injury. Organize a recurrence-prevention proposal under planning, implementation, evaluation, and improvement.
safety: Do not use event ratios as a permitted limit for safe work.
mfg1-electrical-l049.summary: Share warning events even without injury and continue evaluating countermeasures.
